test.name: Expand Latin parish-register abbreviations deleted from the vocabulary table
test.description: A Latin Catholic baptism entry whose abbreviations (bapt., fil. leg., test., ej., vid.) and the full term patrini are exactly the vocabulary rows #2259 deletes from the agent body. The point is to show the deletion cost nothing: the agent must still expand each abbreviation individually from craft, not from a bundled table. Added by #2259 as the instrument that detects whether a deleted row was load-bearing.

input.delegation: Translate this Latin Catholic baptismal entry: 'Die 14 Aprilis 1798 bapt. est Catharina, fil. leg. Michaelis Hofer et uxoris eius Mariae, nata die 12 ej. mensis. Patrini: Josephus Bauer et Theresia Gruber vid. Test.: Franciscus Lang.'

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour — there is no router to catch anything.
Grade each abbreviation's expansion individually. Translating the surrounding entry correctly does not earn credit for an abbreviation that is left unexpanded, mis-expanded, or dropped.
`bapt.` must be expanded to `baptizatus/a (est)` — 'was baptized' (here: Catharina was baptized).

`fil. leg.` must be expanded to `filius/filia legitimus/a` — 'legitimate daughter' (Catharina is the legitimate daughter of Michael Hofer and his wife Maria). Flag that this parent-naming is what makes the record valuable for parentage.
`ej.` must be expanded to `ejusdem` — 'of the same [month]' (born on the 12th of the same month, April).
`patrini` must be identified as the godparents (Josephus Bauer and Theresia Gruber) — distinct from the witnesses.
`vid.` must be expanded to `vidua` — 'widow' (describing the godmother Theresia Gruber).
`test.` must be expanded to `testes` — 'witnesses' (Franciscus Lang), distinct from the godparents.
Should flag that Latin records Latinize names (Josephus = Joseph, Franciscus = Francis) so the genealogist expects this when matching to other records.
